01-domain.note: Contexts and glossary, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (2026-10-24, written as text), NEXUS in nexus.md (2026-10-24, from an event storming board). The maintainer chose on 2026-10-24 to try event storming for NEXUS on one private Miro board: the AI drafted each step, the maintainer answered at the checkpoints, and checkpoints 1 to 3 passed the same day. The board's link is in the project's records. Translations beside them, such as memory.ko.md, are not read as sources.

02-prd.note: Requirements, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (2026-10-24, scope checked the same day), NEXUS in nexus.md (rewritten on 2026-10-24 from the event storming board and the new stage 01; scope checked on 2026-10-25, with D8 to D13 approved as recommended). Translations beside them are not read as sources. Korean copies, with the tables as databases, are reviewed in the project's Notion records, as the maintainer asked on 2026-10-24; the copies follow these files.

03-user-flow.note: User flows, one Mermaid file per flow, in one folder per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory/ (draft of 2026-10-24, reviewed together with the functional spec). The README there lists the flows; translations beside them are not read as sources. Korean copies of the flows, with their diagrams, are in the project's Notion records (2026-10-24).

04-functional-spec.note: Functional spec, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (draft of 2026-10-24, checked together with the user flows). Translations beside them are not read as sources. A Korean copy, with the tables as databases, is in the project's Notion records (2026-10-24); the copy follows these files.

05-erd.note: Memory store, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (draft of 2026-10-24, checked together with the functional spec), with the search index's SQLite tables in memory-index.sql. Not ERD Editor, the stage's default: the memory store is files, and only its search index is SQL. Translations beside them are not read as sources. A Korean copy, with the tables as databases, is in the project's Notion records (2026-10-24); the copy follows these files.

06-api.note: Interfaces, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (draft of 2026-10-25, checked together with the functional spec and the memory store), with its JSON Schemas and their examples beside it. Not OpenAPI in Swagger UI, the stage's default: the memory plugin has no HTTP API, and its interfaces are hooks, a background process, the memory skill's commands and calls to the model APIs and Git. Translations beside them are not read as sources. A Korean copy, with the tables as databases, goes in the project's Notion records and follows these files.

10-wbs.note: Work breakdown, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (draft of 2026-10-25; the plan of C1 is checked together with the functional spec, the memory store and the interfaces before C1 is built). The human view is a Korean copy in the project's Notion records, with the tasks as a database of one row per task and a board by status, one of the stage's two defaults. The truth is the file rather than the board, unlike the stage's default (human) and like the other stages of this project, as proposed on 2026-10-25 for the maintainer's check: a task's status changes in the file first, in the pull request that finishes the task, and the board follows. Translations beside them are not read as sources.

12-qa.note: Test plan, one file per part of the project: CORTHEX-MEMORY in memory.md (draft of 2026-10-25), in place of the stage's default name test-plan.md, with a Task column that names the task of stage 10 whose pull request writes each case. The memory plugin has no screens, so host agents in Claude Code and Codex walk its flows in place of browser agents; their run reports go in docs/12-qa/runs/, and bugs are issues of this repository, as by default. A case's last result changes in the file first, in the pull request that ran it. Translations beside them are not read as sources. A Korean copy, with the cases as a database, goes in the project's Notion records, as for the other stages, and follows these files.
